assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Ductile
items.clue: Able to be drawn into wires, because layers of ions slide.

items.label: Octet rule
items.clue: The tendency of atoms to end up with eight outer electrons.

items.label: Malleable
items.clue: Able to be hammered into shape, because layers of ions slide.

items.label: Lone pair
items.clue: Two outer electrons on an atom that are not shared with another atom.

questions.stem: Nitrogen monoxide, NO, is a gas whose molecules have a total of 11 valence electrons. Which statement best describes how well the Lewis structure model, with its octet rule, represents NO?

options.text: It is adequate: a triple bond and one lone pair on each atom give both atoms an octet.
It is limited: it leaves N without an octet, yet each atom in a real molecule must have one.
It is adequate: with the unpaired electron on N, both formal charges are zero, so it is complete.
It is limited: an odd number of electrons cannot all be paired, so one atom lacks an octet.

questions.explanation: Lewis structures pair electrons. With 11, one is unpaired and both atoms can't have eight.

questions.stem: Four solids, P, Q, R and S, are tested. - P: melts at 801 °C; conducts when molten but not as a solid; dissolves in water. - Q: melts at 1085 °C; conducts as a solid and when molten; insoluble in water. - R: melts at 114 °C; does not conduct as a solid or when molten; insoluble in water. - S: melts at 1710 °C; does not conduct as a solid or when molten; insoluble in water. Which pairing of substance and structure is correct?

options.text: P is metallic, because it conducts when molten.
Q is ionic, because it conducts when molten.
R is molecular, because it melts low and never conducts.
S is ionic, because its melting point is very high.

questions.stem: Hydrogen cyanide, H–C≡N, has a carbon–nitrogen triple bond. Methylamine, CH₃–NH₂, has a carbon–nitrogen single bond. How does the C≡N bond compare with the C–N bond?

options.text: It is longer and weaker, as six electrons between the nuclei repel each other.
It is the same length and strength, as both bonds join the same two elements.

questions.explanation: Three shared pairs between C and N attract both nuclei more strongly than one pair does, pulling them closer. Shorter and stronger.

questions.stem: Each liquid is tested with two electrodes and a bulb. Which liquid will not conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: TiCl₄ (boils at 136 °C) is made of small covalent molecules. With no ions and no delocalised electrons, nothing carries charge, even though titanium is a metal.
